title: Valid Palindrome
summary: Decide whether a phrase reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring punctuation and case.
statement:
A phrase is a **palindrome** if, after converting all uppercase letters to lowercase and removing
every character that is not a letter or digit, it reads the same forwards and backwards.

Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome and `false` otherwise.
An empty string (or one with no letters or digits) counts as a palindrome.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

hints: Could you compare characters from both ends without building a cleaned-up copy of the string first?
Move two pointers inward. Skip anything that isn't a letter or digit (Character.isLetterOrDigit), and compare with Character.toLowerCase.

left = 0, right = s.length - 1
while left < right:
    while left < right and s[left] is not alphanumeric: left++
    while left < right and s[right] is not alphanumeric: right--
    if lower(s[left]) != lower(s[right]): return false
    left++, right--
return true

Building a filtered, lowercased copy and comparing it with its reverse is correct but uses O(n) extra memory. Two pointers that skip non-alphanumeric characters do the same check in place: O(n) time, O(1) space. Keep the `left < right` guard in the inner skip loops, or a string of only punctuation will run the pointers past each other.

input.s: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
